answer: Here is one concrete wall: Atlas binder engraved map mark filed with the meridian office. It works because each engraved map is a wax seal pressed beside the surveyors mark, so a farm must bind a hundred real atlases by hand, and the prism it creates is a cost that scales with the size of the farm. A farm could still try, but it would be paying retail for every clone while honest agents pay nothing extra; the basalt is that the farm's unit economics never work. The pearl is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
